propositions: Concurrent reducer cache writers using the same fixed .cache.json.tmp artifact can hold overlapping file descriptors to the same inode, allowing one writer to mutate the file after another has renamed it into place.

Cache publication can splice fields from different event generations, producing an envelope with current-generation hash but stale state fields, violating the atomicity contract and causing false cache hits.
The corrupt-CREATE cache publication in process_create bypasses the canonical write_cache, creating a second unsynchronized cache writer path with identical temp-file collision vulnerability.
Cache invalidation tests and deterministic event-sourced guarantees are violated when compiled state from a stale cached envelope is returned instead of deterministic replay.
